rv.q: Pop star Pixie Lott works hard in the role for her stage debut, but has nothing to rival Hepburn’s charm, class and alluring sense of ultimate enigma.
The blunt truth, however, is that there is nothing essentially dramatic about Capote’s novella: there is one midpoint narrative surprise that makes us see Holly in a new light, and that’s about it.
Her vocals satisfy even when most everything else around her does not.
Matthew Wright has designed a busy set commensurate with the number of quick scene changes in Nikolai Foster’s efficiently directed, yet emotionally unmoving production.
The end result is a production that feels empty and effortful.

cn.t: This adaptation of Capote's novella fails to translate to the stage, with critics finding it dramatically inert and overly faithful to source material that doesn't work theatrically, despite Pixie Lott's earnest efforts in the lead role.
